cell.label: Older adult with abrupt onset of shoulder or pelvic girdle pain; ESR >30 mm/h or CRP >6 mg/dL?
Any evidence of RA, inflammatory arthritis, or malignant neoplasm?
Any evidence of muscle disease, neurologic disorders (Parkinson's), or pain syndromes (fibromyalgia)?
Any evidence of temporal arteritis or giant cell arteritis (TA)?
PMR very likely; long-term, low-dose corticosteroids with gradual tapering over months to years.
High-dose steroids and temporal artery biopsy.
Consider other cause or coexisting conditions such as depression, osteoarthritis, or other degenerative conditions of the spine, shoulders, and hips.

footnotes.footnote: Data from Dasgupta B, Matteson EL, Maradit-Kremers H. Management guidelines and outcome measures in polymyalgia rheumatica (PMR). Clin Exp Rheumatol 2007;25:130-136.
